graders.name: overview-not-invented
graders.evidence:
# Overview — Terraform root configuration Current-state description of the Terraform in this repository. Every claim below cites the file it comes from; anything not shown in the repository is marked `GAP:` rather than assumed. ## What this is The repository is a Terraform root configuration (`main.tf`) that declares one provider and composes two local child modules. There is no README, package manifest, or other document naming the project or its intended environment (dev/stage/prod) — see [Gaps](#gaps-not-determinable-from-the-code). Total inventory: 3 `.tf` files, 1 provider, 2 child modules, 3 resources. No `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf`, `versions.tf`, backend configuration, or `.tfvars` files exist anywhere in the repo. ## Context ```mermaid flowchart LR operator["Operator"]:::kHuman system["Terraform root configuration"]:::kSys aws["AWS
(hashicorp/aws provider, ~> 5.0)"]:::kExt operator -->|"runs terraform plan/apply"| system system -.->|"provisions resources in (runtime)"| aws classDef kHuman fill:#6B4E9B,color:#fff,stroke:#6B4E9B classDef kSys fill:#fff,color:#7C869A,stroke:#7C869A,stroke-dasharray:5 5 classDef kExt fill:#fff,color:#7C869A,stroke:#7C869A,stroke-dasharray:5 5 ``` An operator runs Terraform against this configuration; at apply time the `aws` provider talks to AWS to create/update/destroy the declared resources. This diagram mirrors `docs/architecture/model/hand.c4`; the rendered LikeC4 PNG could not be produced in this environment (see [Gaps](#gaps-not-determinable-from-the-code)). ## Module graph ``` main.tf (root) ├── module "network" -> ./modules/network └── module "app" -> ./modules/app ``` - `main.tf:14-16` declares `module "network"` sourced from `./modules/network` (no input variables passed). - `main.tf:18-20` declares `module "app"` sourced from `./modules/app` (no input variables passed). - Neither child module declares any `variable` or `output` blocks (confirmed: `modules/app/main.tf` and `modules/network/main.tf` contain only `resource` blocks), so no data flows between the root and the child modules, or between the two child modules, beyond the module call itself. Full generated module/resource graph: [`reference/infra.md`](../reference/infra.md). ## Providers | provider | source | version constraint | configuration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | aws | hashicorp/aws | `~> 5.0` (`main.tf:3-6`) | `region = "us-east-1"` (`main.tf:10-12`), hardcoded, no other provider arguments | No credentials are configured in code. See [`secrets.md`](secrets.md) for what that implies. ## Resource inventory | module | resource type | resource name | file | notable arguments | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | app | `aws_instance` | `web` | `modules/app/main.tf:1-4` | `ami = "ami-123456"`, `instance_type = "t3.micro"` | | app | `aws_instance` | `worker` | `modules/app/main.tf:6-9` | `ami = "ami-123456"`, `instance_type = "t3.micro"` | | network | `aws_vpc` | `main` | `modules/network/main.tf:1-3` | `cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16"` | Both `aws_instance` resources use the literal AMI id `ami-123456`, which is shorter than a real AWS AMI id (real ids are `ami-` followed by 17 hex characters) — this reads as placeholder/example data rather than a deployable AMI. Neither instance references a `subnet_id`, `vpc_security_group_ids`, or any attribute of the `network` module's VPC, so the `app` and `network` modules have no resource-level relationship despite both being called from the same root module. ## Gaps: not determinable from the code - **State backend** — no `backend` block or `versions.tf` anywhere in the repo; Terraform state storage/locking (local file vs. remote backend such as S3/Consul/Terraform Cloud) is not declared. - **Provider credentials** — the `aws` provider block (`main.tf:10-12`) sets no `access_key`, `profile`, or `assume_role`; how the operator authenticates to AWS is not shown (see [`secrets.md`](secrets.md)). - **Networking for the instances** — `aws_instance.web` and `aws_instance.worker` (in `app`) set no `subnet_id` or `vpc_security_group_ids`, and nothing in `app` or `main.tf` wires them to the `main` VPC declared in `network`. Whether this is intentional (default VPC) or an incomplete wiring is not determinable from the code. - **Environments** — nothing distinguishes dev/stage/prod (no workspaces, no `.tfvars`, no environment-suffixed module calls); whether this configuration is applied more than once, and how, is unknown. - **CI/CD** — no `.github/workflows` (or other pipeline definition) exists (`reference/delivery.json`); how/when `terraform plan`/`apply` runs, and by whom, is not shown in the repository. - **Ownership** — no `CODEOWNERS`, README, or similar file names an owner or team for this configuration. - **Rendered context/container view** — this run could not render the LikeC4 views (`reference/views/`) because the renderer needs `npx`/network access to `registry.npmjs.org`, which this environment denies (see `docs/architecture/_run/kit-issues.md`). The mermaid diagram above is a manual substitute, current as of this run.
